items.q: Quandō multae nāvēs multīque nautae in marī pereunt?
items.en: When do many ships and many sailors perish at sea?
items.hint: an adverb of time

items.en: How highly do merchants value the life of sailors?
items.hint: a genitive of value with aestimāre (magnī / parvī)

items.q: Cūr nōnnūllī mercātōrēs ipsī in terrās aliēnās nāvigant?
items.en: Why do some merchants themselves sail to foreign lands?
answers: quod mercēs pretiōsās nautīs crēdere nōlunt
quia mercēs pretiōsās nautīs crēdere nōlunt
items.hint: a quod clause; crēdere ('entrust') takes the dative (nautīs)

items.q: Cūr mercātor mercēs pretiōsās omnī pecūniā suā ēmerat?
items.en: Why had the merchant bought precious wares with all his money?
answers: ut eās māiōre pretiō in Graeciā vēnderet
eō cōnsiliō ut eās māiōre pretiō in Graeciā vēnderet
choices: ut eās māiōre pretiō in Graeciā vēnderet
items.hint: eō cōnsiliō ut + imperfect subjunctive (a purpose clause); māiōre pretiō is an ablative of price

items.en: What has the merchant suddenly become?
items.hint: a superlative predicate nominative after factus est

items.q: Utrum miserius est: dīvitiās āmittere an līberōs āmittere?
items.en: Which is more wretched: to lose wealth or to lose children?
items.hint: an infinitive phrase as subject; multō + comparative = 'much more …'

items.en: What had the helmsman himself ordered?
items.hint: imperāvit ut + imperfect subjunctive passive (iacerentur)

items.en: How was the ship saved?
items.hint: an ablative of means with a genitive attached (iactūrā mercium)

items.en: Why did the sailors throw the wares overboard?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive of esse

items.en: None of the sailors died, did they?
items.hint: num expects 'no'; nostrum is a partitive genitive ('of us')

items.q: Quandō līberī gubernātōris māximā laetitiā afficiuntur?
items.en: When are the helmsman's children filled with the greatest joy?
answers: cum patrem suum salvum redīre vident
cum patrem ē nāvigātiōne perīculōsā salvum redīre vident
choices: cum patrem suum salvum redīre vident
items.hint: a cum clause with the present indicative (a repeated occasion); afficī takes an ablative (laetitiā)

items.en: What does the distraught man ask himself?
answers: utrum in mare saliat an in nāve remaneat
utrum in mare saliat an in nāve maneat
utrum in mare saliat an in nāve remaneat sē interrogat
items.hint: an indirect double question: utrum … an + present subjunctive, inside a result clause (ita … ut)

items.en: By what was Arion saved?
items.hint: an ablative with a passive verb (an animal as the means, no ā/ab)

items.en: How beautifully did Arion sing to the lyre?
answers: tam pulchrē ut alter Orpheus appellārētur
tam pulchrē ut alter Orpheus appellārētur canēbat
choices: tam pulchrē ut alter Orpheus appellārētur
tam male ut nēmō eum audīret
tam clārā vōce ut piscēs fugerent
items.hint: a result clause: tam … ut + imperfect subjunctive

items.q: Cūr bēstiae ferae ad Orpheum accēdēbant?
items.en: Why did wild beasts come up to Orpheus?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive (canentem is a present participle agreeing with eum)

items.en: When did the sailors decide to kill Arion?
answers: cum ex Italiā in Graeciam nāvigāret
cum ex Italiā in Graeciam nāvigāret magnāsque dīvitiās sēcum habēret
choices: cum ex Italiā in Graeciam nāvigāret
items.hint: a circumstantial cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive

items.en: Why did the poor sailors envy Arion?
items.hint: invidēre takes the dative; tap the adjective that gives the reason (hominī dīvitī)

items.en: What did the sailors order Arion to do?
items.hint: imperāvērunt ut + imperfect subjunctive; ita permōtī … ut before it is a result clause

items.q: Quōmodo Arīōn piscēs ad nāvem allēxit?
items.en: How did Arion lure the fish to the ship?
items.hint: the gerund in the ablative (means: 'by singing')

items.en: Who came up under the swimming man?
items.hint: the nominative subject; cantū allectus is a perfect participle agreeing with it

items.en: Where did Arion go straight away from there?
items.hint: the accusative of a city name for place to which (no preposition)

items.en: What did the king ask the sailors?
answers: num scīrent ubi esset Arīōn et quid faceret
ubi esset Arīōn et quid faceret
num scīrent ubi Arīōn esset et quid faceret
items.hint: indirect questions: num / ubi / quid + imperfect subjunctive after a past verb of asking

items.q: Quandō nautae maleficium suum cōnfessī sunt?
items.en: When did the sailors confess their crime?
answers: cum eum quem mersum esse putābant ita vīvum appārēre vidērent
items.hint: a cum clause with the imperfect subjunctive; inside it an accusative + infinitive (eum … appārēre)

items.en: What does this story warn us to do?
answers: ut semper bonō animō sīmus nēve umquam dē salūte dēspērēmus
ut bonō animō sīmus nēve dē salūte dēspērēmus
choices: ut semper bonō animō sīmus nēve umquam dē salūte dēspērēmus
items.hint: monēmur ut … nēve + present subjunctive (present main verb)

items.en: What does Medus confess?
answers: sē pecūniam ē sacculō dominī surripuisse
sē pecūniam ē sacculō dominī surripuisse cōnfitētur
items.hint: an indirect statement with sē and a perfect infinitive (surripuisse) after a deponent verb

items.en: Why did Medus steal his master's coins?
answers: eō cōnsiliō ut dōnum pretiōsum emeret
eō cōnsiliō ut dōnum pretiōsum Lydiae emeret
items.hint: eō cōnsiliō ut + imperfect subjunctive (purpose)

items.q: Quid Lydia in mare abicere vult?
items.en: What does Lydia want to throw into the sea?
items.hint: the accusative object of gerere and abiciam

items.en: Where was Polycrates' ring found?
items.hint: in + ablative for place where (nōn in …, sed in …)

items.en: Why did Polycrates throw away his ring?
answers: cum sēsē nimis fēlīcem esse cēnsēret
cum sē nimis fēlīcem esse cēnsēret
quia sē nimis fēlīcem esse cēnsēbat
quod sē nimis fēlīcem esse cēnsēbat
items.hint: a causal cum clause ('since') with the imperfect subjunctive, containing an indirect statement (sēsē … esse)

items.q: Quis Polycratī suāsit ut iactūram faceret?
items.en: Who urged Polycrates to make a sacrifice of something?
items.hint: the nominative subject; suādēre takes the dative and ut + subjunctive

items.q: Quālis erat piscis quem piscātor cēpit?
items.en: What was the fish like that the fisherman caught?
items.hint: the adjective before the result clause tam … ut (+ imperfect subjunctive)

items.q: Nōnne Polycratēs beātissimus omnium fuit, ut Mēdus dīcit?
items.en: Wasn't Polycrates the happiest of all, as Medus says?
answers: Ita, nēmō umquam eō tyrannō beātior fuit
Nēmō umquam eō tyrannō beātior fuit
Ita, nēmō umquam eō beātior fuit
items.hint: nōnne expects 'yes'; eō tyrannō is an ablative of comparison after beātior

items.q: Unde nāvis vēlōx nāvī Mēdī appropinquat?
items.en: From where is the fast ship approaching Medus' ship?
items.hint: ā + ablative ('from the north'); appropinquāre takes the dative (nōbīs)

items.q: Quid gubernātor imperat, cum vēla scissa sint?
items.en: What does the helmsman order, since the sails are torn?
items.hint: imperat ut + present subjunctive passive (agātur); rēmīs is an ablative of means
